newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa, SAS cooperate in freight.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa, SAS cooperate in freight.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG said on Thursday its Lufthansa cargo freight unit had agreed to cooperate with Scandinavian Airlines System's SAS Cargo, starting with joint sales operations.
The cooperation, which follows the wider alliance between the two airlines launched in January 1996, is aimed at achieving greater cost efficiencies, Lufthansa said in a statement.
Lufthansa said the collaboration would later extend to marketing functions and joint development of new products, leading to sharing of freight capacity and fully communal freight services by 2000.
Lufthansa said the two would offer services together at the new Oslo airport to be opened in late 1998.
The alliance will be managed by a steering committee led by Lufthansa Cargo management chairman Wilhelm Althen and SAS Cargo vice president and general manager Peter Gronlund.
Lufthansa was not immediately available to comment on a report that it was planning a global airline alliance with eight other major airlines.
